text:
Maya: quick follow-up from yesterday's paged-KV + attention kernel sync. main problem: eviction + fragmentation creates non-contiguous KV ranges which break the fast kernels that assume contiguous KV slices. want to capture tradeoffs and next steps.

Tom: which kernels specifically fail or degrade the most? flashattention? blocked attention?

Maya: blocked/blocked-fused kernels that vectorize loads per head are the worst. flash variants expect contiguous key/value bytes for the per-layer cache; if we return scattered pages they fall back to gather code paths with big perf hit.

Priya: to add: our current gather fallback is unoptimized — pointer chasing + smaller SIMD batches. when fragmentation > ~25% we see latency p99 regressions.

Javier: high level options we discussed:
  1) background compaction: keep pages simple, periodically defrag to restore contiguous regions. cheap background but can cause short pauses and write amplification.
  2) indirection table: maintain a logical->physical page map and add scatter/gather support in the kernel (or a thin runtime shuffler). keeps eviction simple but adds indirection overhead and cache pressure.
  3) allocation/pinning policies: reserve contiguous runs for "hot" models/requests and only page others. more complex allocator and fragmentation-aware heuristics.

Maya: here's a possible eviction config sketch to discuss (informal):

```yaml
eviction_policy:
  mode: lru_pages
  safe_margin_ms: 200   # keep some headroom for in-flight requests
  compaction_rate: 0.1  # fraction of pages compacted per cycle
  max_fragmentation: 0.3
  reserve_contiguous_bytes: 1MB  # for kernels that need a run
```

Tom: any numbers for the perf delta between contiguous vs scattered?

Maya: ran a quick microbench on an A100: contiguous per-layer KV path = baseline. using the current scatter fallback gives ~1.8x token latency and ~2.2x lower throughput under sustained load. indirection table + a kernel rewrite (scatter-gather in kernel) looks like ~30% overhead vs contiguous in our prototype, but still much better than the user-space gather fallback.

Priya: so indirection + kernel scatter/gather seems promising but needs careful L1/L2 locality testing. and we should expose kernel capability flags so runtime can pick the right code path.

Javier: +1 for capability flags. recommend adding:
  - kernel.capabilities = ["contiguous_kv", "scatter_gather_kv"]
  - model.annotations: prefers_contiguous_kv = true/false
  - router policy: if model requires_contiguous_kv and fragmentation high -> route to compaction/priority pool or fallback model variant

Maya: agreed. also note cost tradeoffs: compaction increases write IOPS and can push more data to NVMe if paging to disk. indirection increases per-request pointer ops and slightly higher L2 miss-rate. allocate based on SLA tier.

runtime-bot: compaction-runner: started compaction on pool-3 at 1758001250, reclaimed 64MB, fragmentation -> 18%.

Maya: action items (I'll open issues):
  - RFC: indirection table + kernel scatter-gather API (owner: Priya, due: EOD Fri)
  - Bench: microbench compaction pause vs throughput, end-to-end p99 impact (owner: Tom)
  - Router: add kernel capability flags + fallback rules, implement simple policy to reserve contiguous runs for high-SLA models (owner: Javier)

Tom: sgtm :thumbsup:

Priya: I'll draft the kernel ABI. quick Q: do we need per-head contiguous guarantees or per-layer is enough? prefer per-layer to keep complexity down.

Javier: per-layer fine to start, we can revisit per-head if we see head-locality wins.

Maya: cool. I'll post links to the prototype bench and the raw traces in #eng-runtime. thanks all.
